scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: Returns arrive
scenes.caption: The library club tests fictional return cards showing page counts and cover damage. Learners trace a sorting rule and tell the librarian where each card belongs. No books move automatically.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Check before comparing
scenes.caption: Some cards have a blank page count. The team sends those to review before arithmetic. Blank does not mean zero pages. Treating unknown information as a small number would create a confident but unsupported shelf decision.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Both conditions matter
scenes.caption: For complete cards, the compact shelf accepts a book only when its page count is at most two hundred AND its cover is undamaged. Otherwise it goes to review. A short damaged book therefore does not qualify for the shelf.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: The exact boundary
scenes.caption: A card says exactly two hundred pages with an undamaged cover. One learner uses less than two hundred and sends it to review. Choose the comparison that matches the librarian’s stated rule rather than silently changing the permitted boundary.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Test the branches
scenes.caption: The team traces three cards: a short intact book, a short damaged book and a book with missing pages information. Their outputs reveal different reasons for review. Keeping the reason beside the result helps diagnose mistakes in the rule.
scenes.dialogue: Output alone can hide the reason.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: A changed policy
scenes.caption: Now the librarian changes the policy: review any damaged cover OR any book above three hundred pages. Missing counts still need review first. Apply the new statement carefully; do not carry the old two-hundred-page cutoff into this different situation.
scenes.dialogue: New requirements need new test cards.
